summary: Delivery1124 future publisher source is isolated from its reviewed SDK profile/preparation source A. The fresh CLI0.4 route is false-default, default-preflight and disabled with selection/forward absent; no actual native IDs or effect authority are inferred. It reuses the existing pinned protected ordered-effect journal and bound-intent fence. Its operation address stays stable across dispatches; content identity and each finite effect record bind the actual original native caller before transport. Unknown sends stop; an old intent plus404 never licenses a resend. Native API600-second/request bounds and the120-second transition-observation window are finite caller limits, not evidence that NuGet indexing finishes within them. A terminal original can continue only through explicit protected-source original-forward admission and retained journal checkpoint: matching old intents settle, remaining sends gain fresh caller custody, and completion requires a freshly native-qualified public-only install/proof. An already attempted readback asset keeps its original frozen proof bytes. Synthetic actual-entry controls include acknowledged visibility expiry, late public matching and lost-asset forwarding; they do not prove real Authority protection, NuGet signature/installation, runtime budgets, publication or consumer adoption. Historical0.3 publisher/admissions and reviewed A remain preserved; native source delivery, both feeds, actual root consumer and a new ordinary operation remain open under the same owner.
title: Fresh SDK publisher retains original custody through delayed visibility
